user.title: Music Assistant Curated Radio
user.description:
Pick the Music Assistant player to watch. When someone picks a song on it by hand, the queue is refilled with recognisable tracks in the same lane.

You will need a free Last.fm API key. [Create one here]({lastfm_url}) and paste the **API key** below; the shared secret is not needed.

data_description.player: The Music Assistant player entity, not the underlying device entity. The Music Assistant instance is worked out from it.
data_description.lastfm_api_key: Used only for similar-artist lookups. Every request is anonymous and read-only.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach Last.fm to check the key. The key may well be fine; try again in a moment.
error.not_music_assistant: That entity does not belong to a Music Assistant config entry.

abort.already_configured: That player is already set up.

data.max_consecutive: Most in a row from one artist
data.artist_strike_limit: Skips in a row before muting an artist
data.bulk_tracks: Leave a foreign queue alone at (tracks)

data_description.seed_lean: Artist radio always builds from the artist you picked and never wanders. Balanced wanders, but stays within the degrees of separation set below. Discovery wanders without limit and will end up somewhere else entirely, which is the point of it.
data_description.familiarity: How strongly artist choice leans toward the well known. Last.fm ranks similar artists by match score, which tracks how recognisable they are. Familiar crowds selection to the top of that ranking, Adventurous ignores it entirely, Balanced sits between. Familiar is the setting that makes this feel like radio rather than a shuffle.
data_description.explicit: Clean only drops anything flagged explicit, which is what you want when younger ears are in the room. Prefer explicit puts the original ahead of the radio edit, so the edit falls outside the per-artist cut rather than being banned: a clean version is usually a separately titled release, so nothing links the two as versions of one song.
data_description.degrees: How far a session may travel from the artist that started it, in the Six Degrees of Kevin Bacon sense: similar artists are one degree out, their similars two. Three keeps a station recognisably about where it began. Ignored by Artist radio, which never wanders, and by Discovery, which is not fenced.
data_description.min_duration: Anything shorter than this is treated as commentary, an interlude or a skit rather than a song. Search returns them alongside the real tracks, because they sit in the same catalogue. Zero accepts everything.
data_description.max_consecutive: How many tracks from the same artist may play back to back. Two keeps an artist station from feeling like a shuffle without letting anyone monopolise the hour.
data_description.track_suppress_days: Skip a song and it will not be queued again for this long. Zero stops remembering skipped songs.
data_description.artist_strike_limit: Skip this many of one artist's tracks in a row and the artist stops being suggested. Consecutive is the point: unlucky picks spread across an evening mean nothing, three in a row means the artist is wrong for the room. Zero disables muting.
data_description.artist_mute_days: How long a muted artist stays out of the similar-artist pool. The artist you pick yourself is never muted.
data_description.refill_threshold: Top the queue up once this many tracks or fewer remain after the one playing.
data_description.history_minutes: How long a title cannot play again at all. Zero disables that window. Separately, and not adjustable, a song heard in the last eight hours waits until its artist has nothing fresh left, so a returning artist plays their other hits first.
data_description.bulk_tracks: A manual pick is one track; a playlist or album is many. A queue is left alone when it holds at least this many tracks nobody here chose, nothing after them is ours either, and its size moved by at least this much. Both tests are needed: loading a playlist usually replaces the queue rather than adding to it, so growth alone misses it, while size alone cannot see a song picked from within a playlist, which barely moves the count and is still a pick. Three is deliberately low, so a five-track playlist is protected as well as a five-hundred-track one. Zero disables the check.
data_description.settle_seconds: How long to wait after a manual pick before rewriting the queue, so the player has time to settle.
data_description.cooldown_entity: If another routine also rebuilds this player's queue on a schedule, point this at it so its rebuild is never mistaken for a manual pick. Leave empty if nothing else touches the queue.
data_description.cooldown_seconds: How long after that routine runs to skip detection entirely.
data_description.provider_filter: Comma-separated provider prefixes to restrict tracks to, for example tidal. Leave empty to allow every provider.
data_description.filter_live: Drop live versions, which rank high in popularity searches but rarely suit background listening.
data_description.filter_remix: Drop remixes and club mixes. Off by default, since a remix is sometimes the version people know. Worth turning on for a station whose era the remixes are not from.
data_description.filter_holiday: Drop Christmas and other holiday content, which a popularity ranking will surface year round.

max_consecutive.name: Most in a row from one artist

reject_playing.name: Skip and do not play again

build_playlist.name: Build playlist
build_playlist.description: Fills a playlist on your music provider with the same music this queues at home, for somewhere Home Assistant cannot reach. Playback is untouched.

config_entry_id.name: Player configuration
config_entry_id.description: Which configured player to act on. Optional when only one is set up.

name.name: Playlist name
name.description: The playlist is refreshed in place if it already exists, so the name stays stable for anything pointing at it.

seed_artist.name: Seed artist
seed_artist.description: The artist to build around. Leave empty to use whatever is playing now.

length.name: Tracks
length.description: How many tracks to put in the playlist. It reseeds as it goes, so a long playlist drifts the way a long evening does.

provider.name: Provider
provider.description: Music provider to create the playlist on, for example tidal. Leave empty to let Music Assistant choose. Tracks are filtered to match, since a provider playlist can only hold that provider's tracks.

search.name: Search
search.description: Searches Music Assistant for songs, so a dashboard can offer a song to start a station from. Returns results; nothing is played.

config_entry_id.name: Player configuration
config_entry_id.description: Which configured player to act on. Optional when only one is set up.

query.name: Search
query.description: Free text: a song title, an artist, or both.

artist.name: Artist
artist.description: Restrict results to one artist. Optional.

allow_track.name: Allow song again
allow_track.description: Releases a song that was skipped, so it can be queued again before its suppression expires.

config_entry_id.name: Player configuration
config_entry_id.description: Which configured player to act on. Optional when only one is set up.

track.name: Song
track.description: The song to allow, as listed on the Muted artists sensor.

unmute_artist.name: Unmute artist
unmute_artist.description: Gives a muted artist another chance straight away, without waiting for the mute to expire.

config_entry_id.name: Player configuration
config_entry_id.description: Which configured player to act on. Optional when only one is set up.

artist.name: Artist
artist.description: The artist to unmute, as listed on the Muted artists sensor.

forget_feedback.name: Forget feedback
forget_feedback.description: Wipes every remembered skip and mute for this player, starting the learning over.

config_entry_id.name: Player configuration
config_entry_id.description: Which configured player to act on. Optional when only one is set up.

run_batch.name: Run batch
run_batch.description: Builds one continuation batch immediately, seeded from whatever is playing.

config_entry_id.name: Player configuration
config_entry_id.description: Which configured player to build a batch for. Optional when only one is set up.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Replace drops everything queued after the current track and starts fresh. Refill appends without touching what is already queued.

unknown_entry.message: No loaded Music Assistant Curated Radio configuration with ID {entry_id}.

entry_required.message: No single player could be chosen for you: either more than one is set up, or none of them is loaded. Name one with config_entry_id.

nothing_playing.message: Nothing is playing, so there is nothing to hold off.

not_suppressed.message: {track} is not currently being held back.

playlist_running.message: A playlist build is already running. It takes a few minutes.

playlists_unsupported.message: This Music Assistant version does not expose playlist management to Home Assistant, so playlists cannot be built. Everything else is unaffected.

playlist_empty.message: Found nothing to put in {name}. Check that something is playing, or pass a seed artist.
